answer: Autonomous agents tracking sable habitats resist Sybil attacks using graph-based trust propagation. Participants route verifiable interaction paths across a peer-to-peer trust trellis anchored by seed nodes to evaluate a candidate's reputation signal. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of cultivating scarce reciprocal relationships with honest nodes to bridge topological cuts. However, peripheral honest agents with sparse connection graphs face high false-rejection rates.
